subject: MSA: indemnity allocation & defense control
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@arkutech.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@arkutech.com
Date: Wed, 3 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA: indemnity allocation & defense control

Hi Jasmine,

Thank you for the draft MSA. A couple of high-priority items came up on our side during legal review and I want to confirm Arkutech's position before pulling our procurement team in.

1) Defense control for third-party IP claims: Our standard is that customer (Arkutech) will retain the right to select counsel for IP claims, subject to Redwood's right to participate and approval of material settlement terms. We have a preference to avoid automatic assignment of defense control to vendor.

2) Indemnity cap carveouts: We need to carve out willful infringement and third-party IP claims from the liability cap and would like explicit language that fees for injunctive relief and replacement costs are not subject to the cap.

3) Insurance / escrow fallback: If Redwood is unwilling to accept uncapped exposure for IP, our fallback is to require an escrow or insurance-backed remedy to ensure timely relief.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the first two points or propose specific counter-language? If not, please flag whether you want to propose payment/escrow alternatives and the timeline for counsel to align.

Appreciate a quick read — procurement is asking for sign-off this week.

Best,
Elena
General Counsel
Arkutech Systems
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@arkutech.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Oct 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA: indemnity allocation & defense control

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers up front and then a proposed path: 

- Defense control: Redwood prefers vendor-led defense for IP claims to ensure coordinated technical response, but we recognize customer concerns around material settlements. We're open to a compromise where Redwood controls the defense but Arkutech has the right to approve any settlement that imposes non-monetary obligations or materially affects Arkutech's business — with approval not to be unreasonably withheld.

- Cap carveouts: Redwood can accept a narrow carveout for willful infringement and proven third-party IP liability, but we need to limit open-ended uncapped exposure.

- Escrow/insurance: We're willing to discuss an insurance-backed top-up or escrow mechanism for high-severity IP exposures if you need to preserve practical remedies.

Next steps I propose: Karthik (legal) and I will review your standard language and send a short counter-markup by EOD tomorrow. If that doesn't land, let's schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call this week.

Looping Karthik for the markup. Neha — tracking internal contracting timeline.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Oct 2028 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Arkutech redline — need legal view (MSA Section 9)

Jasmine / Neha — read Arkutech's redline. High-level position and suggested counter language below. I also attached a short counter-markup.

High-level points:
- Defense control: Acceptable compromise — Redwood will control the defense for third-party IP claims, provided Arkutech has the right to (i) participate with counsel of its choice at its cost, and (ii) withhold consent to any settlement that imposes non-monetary obligations on Arkutech or requires Arkutech to take affirmative actions unrelated to the claim. Add a requirement that Redwood must notify Arkutech within 5 business days of receipt of any claim and provide material case updates.

- Cap carveouts: Do not accept uncapped exposure for broad categories. We can agree to carve out proven willful infringement and final judgments for third-party IP liability, but with a monetary cap equal to 3x the fees paid under the applicable order form in the prior 12 months (or $5M, whichever is higher). This provides predictability while acknowledging severity.

- Injunctive relief / replacement costs: Agree to contractual language that allows for equitable relief (injunctive) without immediate monetary cap, but Redwood should have rights to cure and substitute functionality where feasible before liability crystallizes.

- Escrow / insurance: Redwood prefers an insurance-backed top-up over operational escrow (logistics, cost). Recommend a cyber/technology errors & omissions rider with a minimum aggregate limit of $5M specifically covering IP claims tied to model outputs. If Arkutech insists on escrow, propose a narrowly scoped escrow (critical model weights or a commercially reasonable cash deposit not exceeding 6 months of fees) with strict release conditions.

Action items: I attached RWI_counter_markups.docx with inline language. If that markup is acceptable, Jasmine please send to Elena with the proposed language and request a 30-minute counsel-to-counsel call if they need clarification. If procurement pushes on uncapped carveouts, we need approval from leadership for any deviation from the 3x/$5M approach.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: RWI_counter_markups.docx
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@arkutech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, contracts@arkutech.com
Date: Sat, 6 Oct 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA: indemnity allocation & defense control — Redwood counterproposal

Elena — thanks for the patience. Attached is a short counter-markup from Redwood addressing the three areas you raised: defense control, carveouts, and an insurance-backed alternative to escrow. Highlights below: 

- Redwood will control defense for third-party IP claims; Arkutech may participate with counsel at its expense and must approve any settlement that imposes non-monetary obligations or material changes to Arkutech's business (approval not to be unreasonably withheld). Redwood must provide written notice within 5 business days of receipt of a claim and give regular updates.

- Carveouts: proven willful infringement and final adjudicated third-party IP liability will be carved out from the general liability cap but subject to a defined cap equal to the greater of (a) 3x fees paid under the order form in the prior 12 months, or (b) $5,000,000. Injunctive relief is available, but Redwood will be afforded an opportunity to cure or substitute functionality prior to payment of damages where commercially feasible.

- Insurance: We propose an E&O/IP rider with a minimum aggregate limit of $5M that expressly covers claims arising from model outputs; if Arkutech insists on escrow we propose a cash deposit equal to no more than 6 months of committed fees, released upon final resolution.

Attached: RWI_counter_markups.docx

If that looks acceptable, can we lock a 30-minute counsel call on Monday (Oct 8) to finalize? Procurement is on standby and would like a dotted line approval to proceed once counsel aligns.

Best regards,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
